entities.summary: Anaxagoras was a Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher born in Clazomenae, Asia Minor, during the 5th century BCE, who came to Athens and was charged with impiety, leading to his exile in Lampsacus. He founded the Academy, one of the earliest institutions of higher learning in the Western world, where he taught his philosophical ideas, including the concept of the Mind as the source of all things and the concept of the unity of all things. His works, such as the “Encomium of Helen’, have had a lasting impact on Western philosophy, influencing notable thinkers like Aristotle and Plato. Anaxagoras' ideas about the harmony of the universe and the concept of the “Unlimited’ have shaped the development of Western philosophy, particularly in the areas of metaphysics and epistemology. His philosophical legacy continues to be studied and debated by scholars today.
